stem:
Compare words letter by letter, ignoring case. A shorter exact prefix comes first.
R1: ferry
R2: fern
R3: fertile
R4: ferret
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: All begin fer. fern has n, before r in ferret/ferry and t in fertile. Between ferret and ferry, e precedes y. Thus R2, R4, R1, R3.

stem:
File by surname, then given name; names are written Surname, Given. Ignore case and commas. A shorter exact field comes first.
R1: Abao, Luz
R2: Abad, Mila
R3: Abad, Lina
R4: Abao, Lia
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: Abad precedes Abao. Within Abad, Lina precedes Mila; within Abao, Lia precedes Luz. Thus R3, R2, R4, R1.

stem:
Local index rule: replace a leading numeral 1 with One, 2 with Two, and 3 with Three before filing. Then compare the resulting names word by word, ignoring case; within a word compare letters alphabetically. A shorter exact word comes first.
R1: 3 Oaks Unit
R2: 2 Bays Unit
R3: 1 Elm Unit
R4: 3 Alders Unit
Which complete filing sequence follows this rule?
explanation: Expand the leading numerals to obtain Three Oaks Unit, Two Bays Unit, One Elm Unit and Three Alders Unit. Alphabetically One precedes Three, which precedes Two. Within the Three group, Alders precedes Oaks. Thus R3, R4, R1, R2. Numeric order would place Two before Three and violate the stated filing convention.

stem:
Compare letter by letter after removing spaces, hyphens and apostrophes; ignore case. Do not expand any word.
R1: Rock Bay
R2: Rock-Bank
R3: Roc Kaba
R4: Rockbar
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: Normalized strings are rockbay, rockbank, rockaba, rockbar. rockaba comes first; then rockbank, rockbar, rockbay by n, r, y. Thus R3, R2, R4, R1.

stem:
Drop initial A, An or The only when it is a separate word. Then compare word by word, ignoring case; shorter exact words come first.
R1: The Anvil Desk
R2: An Amber Desk
R3: A Anchor Desk
R4: The Amber Desks
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: After dropping articles, compare Amber Desk, Amber Desks, Anchor Desk, Anvil Desk. Desk precedes Desks; Amber precedes Anchor and Anvil. Thus R2, R4, R3, R1.

stem:
Compare word by word after expanding Dept. to Department. Ignore periods and case. Do not alter any other words. Shorter exact words come first.
R1: Dept. Art
R2: Departmental Aid
R3: Department Arts
R4: Dept. Archive
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: Expanded Department precedes Departmental. Within Department, Archive precedes Art, and Art precedes Arts as a shorter exact word. Thus R4, R1, R3, R2.

stem:
File by surname then given name, as written around the comma. Ignore case, spaces and apostrophes WITHIN each field; keep surname particles in place. If both fields tie, use ascending numeric staff ID.
R1: Van Dae, Li; ID12
R2: Vandae, Li; ID3
R3: Van Dam, Lia; ID1
R4: Van Dae, Lia; ID8
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: R1/R2 share normalized surname vandae and given name li; numeric 3 precedes 12. Lia follows Li, and vandam follows vandae. Thus R2, R1, R4, R3.

stem:
Treat abbreviations literally. Compare word by word, ignoring periods and case. A shorter exact word comes first; spaces stay word boundaries.
R1: C. D. Supply
R2: Cedar Depot
R3: C. Depot Supply
R4: C. D. Supplies
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: The first word C precedes Cedar. In C names, second word D precedes Depot. Between Supplies and Supply, i precedes y. Thus R4, R1, R3, R2.

stem:
Drop an initial The. Expand St. to Saint ONLY at the start of the remaining name. Then remove spaces, periods and hyphens and compare letter by letter, ignoring case. If normalized names tie, use ascending numeric branch.
R1: The St. Elmo Hall; branch 14
R2: Saint-Elmo Hall; branch 2
R3: St. Elm Hall; branch 7
R4: Saint Elmo Hall Annex; branch 1
R5: Stanton Hall; branch 3
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: R3 normalizes saintelmhall, before saintelmohall because h precedes o. R1/R2 tie as saintelmohall and branch 2 precedes 14. R4 extends that name and follows both; stantonhall follows saint… names. Thus R3, R2, R1, R4, R5.

stem:
File surname first, given name second, then ascending numeric ID. Ignore initial titles Dr./Ms./Mr.; remove spaces, hyphens and apostrophes within each name field; ignore case. Do NOT expand initials. A shorter exact field precedes its extension.
R1: Dr. De-Sil, An; ID20
R2: Ms. Desil, Ana; ID1
R3: Mr. De Sil, An; ID4
R4: Dr. Desila, A; ID2
R5: Ms. De'Sil, A; ID30
R6: Mr. Desil, An; ID12
Which complete sequence is correct?
explanation: All but R4 have surname desil; R4 desila follows them. Within desil, A precedes An, and An precedes Ana. The three An records use IDs 4,12,20. Thus R5, R3, R6, R1, R2, R4.
